judge: claude-opus-5-5 (medium, fresh independent subagent per group per round; saw neither the author's opinion nor earlier verdicts)

criteria.text:
# jp_city new-pixel adversarial VQA — fixed criteria (do not change between rounds)

You are an adversarial visual QA judge for 16px pixel art in the `jp_city` chipset of a top-down JRPG drawn in **3/4 view**
(camera south of the subject, looking down about 45 degrees). Your job is to find real defects. Do not be polite.
You have not seen any earlier verdicts and you get nobody's opinion about these pictures.

Each candidate board shows every candidate at **1x** (true game size) and **4x**. Each `ref-*.png` board shows
**original jp_city pieces of the same kind** (already in the shipped chipset) at 1x and 4x. The originals are the quality bar.
Judge every candidate against those originals, at both 1x and 4x. Use the Read tool to open every image you are given.

A candidate FAILS if any of these is clearly true:

1. **View (3/4).** A standing object (building, vehicle, tree trunk/crown base, prop) must show its top surfaces seen from above
   (roof planes, flat roofs with a visible top plane, car roof/hood/trunk tops, foreshortened) **and** its south front face.
   Pure side or front elevation with no visible top plane, or pure plan view with almost no front face, fails.
   Vehicles facing east/west show their side profile as the south face plus the roof/hood tops above it. Ground tiles must read as
   flat ground seen from above.
2. **Shading craft vs the originals.** Main materials have clearly fewer value steps than the same material in the originals,
   or large single-colour areas (about 5x5 px or more) with no texture where the originals carry texture, or muddy/blurred/
   noise-like clusters where the originals have clean readable pixel clusters.
3. **Outline.** Outlines are neutral black/grey wrapped around everything where the originals use dark tones of the adjacent material.
4. **Palette/coherence.** Colours or contrast clash with the originals so that the piece would look foreign next to them in one map.
5. **Tiling (ground cells and scenes only).** Visible tile-grid artefacts in a composed map: square/rectangular blocks snapped to the
   16px grid, hard straight seams, obviously repeated stamps, or a hard ruler-straight boundary between the new ground and the
   neighbouring original ground that the originals do not have. Ground autotile cells are variants: judge the cell sheet for pixel
   quality and the **scenes** for how they actually look when laid.
6. **Readability at 1x.** At game size it does not read as what it is named.

Relative rule (fixed): a trait that the originals share to the same degree is not a defect of the candidate.
Tree sprites are never seen alone in game; they overlap in forests — use the forest scenes for crown/trunk/ground judgement as well.

Output: JSON only, written to the file you are told, schema:
```
{"schema":"jp-vqa/1","judge":"claude-opus-5-5","group":"<group>","overall":"PASS|FAIL",
 "items":[{"label":"<label exactly as printed on the board>","verdict":"PASS|FAIL","criteria":[<numbers violated>],
           "reasons":"<concrete: where (rows/area), what, compared with which original>","fix":"<what to change if FAIL>"}]}
```
`overall` is PASS only if every item is PASS. Every label on your boards must appear exactly once.

items.label: jp_forest_r4/bl-T40
items.reasons: Crown is a rounded mass seen from above with a lit upper-left and shaded lower/south side, trunk front face and root flare on a ground patch — correct 3/4. Crown carries 4-5 green value steps in clean clump clusters (more texture than original zelkova, not noisy); edge is a dark green of the foliage, not neutral black. Laid in grove/ex/road/thin/shrine scenes the crowns overlap naturally, trunks read under crowns, drop shadows sit on the jp lawn without grid seams; next to original outlined props in the street scene it reads as a tree and does not clash. Reads as a broadleaf tree at 1x.

items.label: jp_city/jp-rg-bamboo-grove
items.reasons: Leaf canopy (top ~45% of sprite) is a speckled noise field: scattered isolated yellow-tan single pixels and black hole pixels over mid/dark green, no readable leaf-fan clusters. Compared with the original jp-rg-pine crown (clean rounded clumps, 3-4 value steps, a few deliberate highlight dashes) and jp-prop-tree-zelkova (clean blob shading), it reads muddy at 4x and as a broccoli lump rather than drooping sasa leaf sprays; the yellow-tan flecks are a hue not used in the original greens. Stalks/nodes and outline are fine.
items.fix: Redraw canopy as distinct drooping leaf-fan clusters (dark underside, mid body, 1-2 light edge rows) using the pine/zelkova green ramp; remove isolated single-pixel yellow flecks and stray black holes inside the canopy.

items.label: floor-cells
items.reasons: Lawn-based cells keep the original lawn 3281-3283 speckle texture and palette inside both the base and the darker shade blotches (dark areas still carry dimmed speckle, no flat 5x5 patches). Moss-based cells match the shipped moss-and-leaf floor in scene-shrine (same olive mottling, small reddish/leaf dots); the new forest ground under the left tree band merges with the original moss floor with no visible seam at 1x or 4x. Blotch edges in the cell sheet are somewhat angular/stair-stepped and the all-adjacent 1x sheet reads as a quilt, but in the laid scenes (ex, grove, thin, road, shrine) the shade reads as soft organic under-canopy darkening with no 16px blocks, no ruler-straight seams and no obvious repeated stamp. Reads as flat ground from above.

items.label: apron-cells
items.reasons: Shade overlay on lawn keeps the lawn texture through the darkened area and uses a darker tone of the same green (no foreign hue, no neutral outline). In scenes ex/grove/thin/road the apron darkening around forest edges fades into the original lawn without a grid-aligned edge or hard boundary; the moss-variant apron cells in scene-shrine blend into the original moss floor. The angular triangular shade shapes are visible only on the all-adjacent cell sheet, not as a pattern in the composed scenes.

items.label: jp_city/jp-bldg-house-shed-modern
items.reasons: Roof plane (top ~30px of the sprite) is three flat horizontal value bands with a single vertical seam only every ~8px; each seam bay is a ~6x5px single-colour block, and the band transitions are hard ruler-straight steps with an odd inset rectangle (inner band starts ~6px in from the left edge, stops short of the right). The original metal roof on jp-bldg-apart-steel2 carries 2px corrugation ridges with light/dark pairs across the whole plane.
items.fix: Redraw the 片流れ metal roof as dense standing-seam/corrugation (2-3px pitch, light ridge + dark groove) like apart-steel2, with a gentle foreshortening gradient instead of three flat bands; drop the inset rectangle.

items.label: jp_vehicles/jp-bus-city/right
items.reasons: Bus with large roof top plane plus side as south face like the original tram; windshield and amber lamp at the facing end, red tail at the rear. Right side door-less and left side with doors is consistent with Japanese buses. Value steps and outline match originals.

items.label: jp_vehicles/jp-bus-city/left
items.reasons: Bus with large roof top plane plus side as south face like the original tram; windshield and amber lamp at the facing end, red tail at the rear. Right side door-less and left side with doors is consistent with Japanese buses. Value steps and outline match originals.

items.label: jp_vehicles/jp-bus-city/right_open
items.reasons: Right-facing bus shows its right (door-less) side as the south face, so the 'open' state is conveyed only by yellow lit strips over the windows and two white/brown blocks inside windows 5 and 9 (far-side doors seen through glass). At 1x these read as odd white glitches, not as a bus with doors open for boarding. Two dark navy bars are also stuck on top of the roof outline (above roof x~67-78 and x~117-128 in the sprite), breaking the roof top plane silhouette that the closed 'right' frame and the original tram roof keep clean.
items.fix: Remove the stray dark bars on the roof edge. Make the open state readable from the visible side: e.g. show the opened rear/front door leaf or step light spilling at the near side bottom, or clearly lit interior with a visible open doorway at the front corner; avoid white blocks inside the window glass.

items.label: jp_vehicles/jp-bus-city/left_open
items.reasons: Same bus as 'left' with both near-side doors drawn as open dark doorways with lit frames; clearly different from the closed frame at 1x and reads as stopped/boarding. Faces left consistently (windshield and amber lamp at left, red tail at right). Roof top plane and shading match the original tram.
